summary.name: Wox
summary.one_liner: Wox is an open-source, cross-platform desktop launcher for Windows, macOS, and Linux that opens apps, finds files, and runs commands, positioned as an alternative to Raycast and Alfred.
use_cases: launch apps and switch windows quickly
run shell commands from a launcher
convert units, currencies, and time zones
summary.what_it_does: Wox is a launcher that opens apps, searches local files and folders, and runs commands from a keyboard shortcut. Built-in modules include application launch and window switching, file search, clipboard history for text and images, a calculator, a unit/currency/date/time-zone converter, web search, URL opening, floating notes, screenshots, timers, and dictation. Further built-ins cover window layouts, browser bookmarks and tabs, emoji, color picking, media control, AI chat and reusable AI commands, shell commands, system commands, themes, and a plugin manager. The page also says plugins can be created with an AI agent, and that settings can be backed up and synced across devices.
notable: Open source and free, described as a native Raycast / Alfred alternative
Plugin system; the page says plugins can be built with an AI agent
Built-in clipboard history, notes, screenshot, timer, dictation and window layout tools
Themes that follow the system appearance or community themes
caveats: Page does not state any paid tiers; the Awesome Mac listing marks it as freeware
Listing describes it as freeware, while the page says open source and free
